author: Erwin Vervaet
html:
Certainly an interesting read! A few remarks/questions:

I must admit I find the value vs. cost evaluation a bit abstract: how can you even assess the value a suite of unit tests might bring over the course of a project? I do fully agree that packaging integration tests as simple unit tests that run with a “mvn verify” brings a lot of value!

What would the performance difference have been if your controller test used H2 with a Postgres dialect rather than a real Postgres in a container? This is a bit of a general gripe I have with Testcontainers: The typical example given is always that of a SQL database, which is a case that has been covered for the most part for more than a decade now with tools like H2. Also, Testcontainers are often problematic in cloud-based CI/CD setups, where you end in a Docker-in-Docker situation.
